security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, when a breakpoint exception is taken due to a debug trigger type that is NOT defined by the Sdtrig specification to write an address to tval/stval (e.g., icount/type=3 triggers, etrigger/type=4, itrigger/type=5, or textra32/textra64-only triggers), the CSR module unconditionally writes the faulting PC or a virtual address into stval instead of leaving it unmodified or writing 0.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR trap-entry write logic for stval on breakpoint exception path that does not gate on trigger type before writing address — search for unconditional stval assignment in Breakpoint/breakpoint exception case of trap dispatch, e.g., when (exceptionType === Breakpoint) stval := pc or vaddr without checking trigger.type or trigger.action semantics from Sdtrig
security_spec.summary: The spec clarification narrows stval address writing to only breakpoint exceptions 'defined to write an address'; hardware that unconditionally writes PC/vaddr to stval for all breakpoint triggers (including icount/etrigger/itrigger) leaks internal control-flow state to supervisor mode through a CSR that should not carry that information
